subject: iceCreamCart
pitch: A cheerful seaside ice cream cart. A mint and cream body with a scalloped striped canopy in pink and white, two big spoked wheels, a push handle, a chrome lid over the freezer, a hand-painted sign shaped like a cone, and a row of giant fake ice cream cones in pastel flavours along the top.
reasoning:
I'm planning the cart prop as a single module, giving it a root joint for safety even though props may not strictly need a skeleton, then sketching dimensions—a body box roughly 1.3-1.4 meters wide along X, deciding orientation and scale before building out the geometry.

Now I'm detailing the full layout: axle position, body dimensions with mint paint and cream trim, a chrome lid with handles, and wheels built from tori rotated to lie flat with spokes radiating from hub to rim.

Then I'm figuring out the wheel colors—coral pink tires with cream rims and white hubs—and designing the canopy as a lathe-based cone shape with alternating pink and white stripes, supported by four corner poles rising from the cart body.

Working out scalloped edge geometry for the canopy rim...

I'll build the canopy from 16 faceted triangular slab panels with alternating colors, and hang scallops under each rim chord with a slight outward lean so they drape naturally off the sloped roof. I'll also add a pom finial sphere on top and consider bunting details.

Now I'm working out the canopy geometry: rim at y=2.15, peak at 2.65, radius 1.05, with four support poles rising to meet the underside of the sloped roof at their corner positions. I'm also thinking about placing a row of oversized decorative ice cream cones along the top of the canopy structure as a playful crown element.

I'll settle on 8 cones placed at alternating rim vertices facing forward for better visibility and manageable cost. For the sign, I'm thinking of a cone-shaped sign mounted on a pole at the front of the body, designed as an ice cream cone silhouette.

I'll build the ice cream silhouette as separate extruded pieces—a triangular cone, a scoop shape with drip details, and a cherry sphere—painting a diagonal waffle lattice onto the cone using the surface coordinates. I'll also add a small "SCOOPS" text banner via an SVG-textured plane mounted on the body's cream front panel.

Now I'm figuring out where to mount this sign on the body's front face, orienting the extrude so the thickness runs along z while sizing the cone sign (tip down, scoop up) to fit within the body's vertical span, centered between the cream side panels.

I'm planning the side decals -- flanking text banners (maybe "Yum!" or "Scoops!" with different SVGs on left and right) -- and then checking wheel clearance against the body's half-width, making sure the axle rod sits just inside the body edge without clipping.

Now I'm raising the body bottom slightly so the axle and wheels tuck in cleanly without the wheels overlapping the body's x-range. Then I'm designing the push handle: twin rods angling up from the body's back corners to a horizontal pink grip cylinder, capped with small sphere knobs at each end.

Since two wheels alone would tip the cart, I'm adding front support legs with rubber foot pads running down to the floor, balancing the load alongside the rear handle. For the lid, I'm keeping it a simple metallic box with a bevel rather than a lathe shape, sized to match the body footprint.

I'm layering a smaller box on top of the base box to suggest a domed lid, adding front handle posts with a crossbar and a round latch, then placing canopy poles with flange discs at their bases where they meet the lid.

I'm considering a cream-white finial sphere with a small cone on top, plus adding cone-shaped ice cream display pieces positioned tip-down around the rim as decorative accents.

Designing the cone pedestals, with a short stem cylinder holding each cone tip-down, topped with a scoop sphere, drip skirt detail, and sprinkle accents in flavors like strawberry pink.

Writing the checker paint logic...

Working out the cone placement on the rim ring, spacing nine cones across a 160° front arc so their scoop diameters don't overlap, then tallying the total cart height with canopy, cones, and finial — landing around 2.9m, a bit tall versus a real cart's 2.4m but close enough to accept.

Now I'm scaling things down slightly: lowering the rim and peak heights, shrinking the pole lengths and recomputing the roof curve at the pole radius to get a tighter top around 2.55m. For the wheels I'm planning the tire as a dark torus, rim ring in coral, twelve cream spokes running from hub to rim, and a pink hub cylinder capped with a sphere, rotated to lie flat with torus radius and tube sized so the tire bottom just touches the ground.

I'm setting up a joint hierarchy so the wheels and lid can animate — a root "cart" joint, wheel joints at the axle positions, and a hinge joint for the lid at the back, assigning bones to parts as needed. For the body, I'm adding cream panel insets on the mint box sides with a mint border and small rivet details for visual interest.

Now I'm adding a pink piping strip along the top edge and scattering small cream polka-dot decals across the mint sides using a procedural spot paint technique. I'm carefully stacking the layered geometry — body box, cream bottom band, pink top band, and the lid — working out their exact vertical positions and thicknesses so each piece sits flush against the next without gaps or overlaps.

I'm designing front-facing decal panels for the sides of the model: cream squares with SVG texture overlays showing playful text like "SCOOPS" on one side and something festive on the other, using simple shapes like hearts and stars with rounded borders to keep the illustration lighthearted and legible at small texture sizes.

For the central sign, I'm positioning it using local x/y axes facing the camera, with the extrusion depth along Z. I'm working out the geometry for a waffle cone shape topped with a scoop (and considering a second smaller scoop), adjusting the cone height and scoop radius so the whole sign fits proportionally within the cream band without overlapping the lid edge.

Now I'm adding a pink outline halo behind the sign by generating a slightly scaled-up, thinner duplicate of the cone and scoop silhouette offset in Z, and building a scallop-edged scoop outline using a parametric loop that varies the radius with angle to create wavy drips along the lower half.

Working out the layering...

The embedding checks out. For the cone surface I'm applying a waffle lattice pattern using the extrude shape's coordinates, coloring the scoop pink with highlights, and considering adding a cherry sphere on top and small white sprinkle specks, though I'll keep those minimal.

Now I'm working out the handle geometry for the cart: rods angling from the body's back top corners up and backward to form the handle grips, with a crossbar connecting them, plus small diagonal brace rods for support. I'm positioning the grip sleeves in cream over pink rods with rounded end caps, checking that the wheel and leg placement keeps the cart balanced front-to-back.

Now I'm defining the front legs with foot discs so they sit flush on the ground, adding the axle with a bracket box mounting it under the body, and setting up canopy support poles that rise from the body corners to a peak ring. For the canopy itself I'm building a faceted dome out of triangular slabs radiating from a central peak point down to a circular rim.

Writing scallop geometry...

Still working through the extrusion geometry...

I'm computing each slab's angular span using the midpoint angle for color matching. I'm also considering adding tiny contrasting pom-pom spheres at each scallop tip for a cute detail, and placing a ring of cone pedestals near the roof rim just inside the edge, calculating their base radius and height against the roof's slope.

Still writing cone geometry...

Adding a final pink topping sphere with a small cone, and a tiny gold bell near the pole for a cute touch -- then deciding to stop adding extras like bunting or a price board to keep things simple. Now I'm setting up a `box` helper for rendering and planning the color palette, keeping total colors within a reasonable limit.

Setting up the joint hierarchy -- wheel joints mirrored left/right off the cart root, a hinge joint for the lid, and figuring out rotation axes so the torus and cylinder hub pieces align correctly.

For the spokes, I'm computing rim points around the hub using polar coordinates for each rod, then adding decal planes with textures for flavor labels mounted flush against the cart panels.

I'm figuring out panel proportions so the mint body color peeks around the decal borders, then considering light speckling or spotting on the body paint for texture without overcomplicating the geometry.

For the scalloped edge of the panel, I'm computing the outline points along an arc to create the wavy cut, using sharp corners at each scallop intersection and checking that the curve stays smooth without self-intersecting.

Now I'm positioning the slab edges at the rim and setting up the cone shapes for the sign and its halo, placing their outline points to form the pointed cone silhouette and a slightly larger scooped halo shape behind it.

I'm computing a star-shaped scoop outline for the sign topper and checking the vertical overlap between the cone and the halo/scoop pieces to make sure they connect without gaps, then verifying the sign's total height stays within the panel bounds while the cherry accent pokes slightly above into the lid band.

Skipping the cherry in favor of a handful of tiny sprinkle boxes scattered on the scoop front for decoration, choosing a light chrome grey for the lid color, and moving into writing out the final export code using a bone-aware part helper where static pieces simply omit the bone parameter.
